nodes.description: Investigational negative allosteric modulators reduce CaSR signaling. A three-day NPSP795 study in five adults increased PTH without significant improvement in ionized calcium or fractional calcium excretion. An uncontrolled encaleret phase 2b study in 13 adults improved serum calcium and hypercalciuria over 24 outpatient weeks. The 2026 CALIBRATE conference report adds randomized phase 3 evidence: at week 24, 75.6% of encaleret participants achieved both blood and urine calcium targets, compared with 19% in the concurrent standard-care group. The primary comparison was separately within the encaleret arm against its own pretreatment standard-care period (75.6% versus 4.4%). These are biochemical endpoints reported in a conference abstract; long-term kidney protection is not established. FDA accepted the encaleret application in July 2026, with approval still pending at review. AXT914 and related quinazolinones have preclinical evidence, not established clinical ADH1 efficacy.

nodes.description: A long-acting PTH(1-34) prodrug approved by the FDA for adult hypoparathyroidism. ADH1-specific evidence remains limited: a broader pivotal trial included very few ADH1 patients, and a 2026 report described off-label treatment of one 16-year-old. Tetany resolved, calcium and phosphate balance improved, and active vitamin D and calcium were stopped while low-dose hydrochlorothiazide, magnesium and potassium continued. Urinary calcium improved in the reported follow-up, but persistent hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia and the uncontrolled design limit claims of complete correction or renal protection. Pediatric efficacy and long-term safety are not established.
